strategies.instructions: Explicitly select the Google-hosted Calendar Developer Preview and its retained Streamable HTTP endpoint. The guide advertises event reads and writes, but its sample OAuth scopes permit only calendar-list reads, event reads and free/busy. The sample does not authorize mutations. Observe current tool schemas and have the credential/policy owner verify the selected account, calendar and operation-specific scopes before binding any operation. Preview eligibility and host-selected prompt/response screening are prerequisites. If setup or authorization is refused, report that result; do not switch to REST.
unresolved_details: Preview membership, permitted preview use, selected project/API enablement, host OAuth registration and account consent are not established by this bundle.

The guide sample uses readonly/freebusy scopes despite advertised write tools. Actual operation authority, current schemas and owner-authenticated role readiness require separate verification; no implicit scope expansion is supplied.
The hosted implementation is mutable. No live Google operation, account isolation, revocation or deployment support assessment is claimed.

strategies.instructions: Explicitly select Python GoogleCalendarOperations in sdk/python with the google-calendar optional profile. Read GOOGLE-CALENDAR.md and this version's SUPPORT.md for the exact retained source checkpoint. The host supplies an authenticated HTTPX client, API base and selected calendar. Coverage is one-page event listing, get, insert, patch and delete; unsupported Calendar options refuse. Preserve exact provider event IDs, ETags and returned versions. A write error or cancellation carries unknown outcome and permits no automatic retry, replacement event ID or fallback. Preserve a host's internal-calendar restrictions, origin stamping, version ledger, deterministic IDs and final readback in their existing owners. This is a separately selected REST strategy; the library does not store credentials, perform OAuth or activate tools.
unresolved_details: The host must bind the selected Python SDK source or separately verified artifact, selected account/calendar, operation schemas and lifecycle to the existing service export. The operation library is not an activated tool surface.

The existing host credential owner must supply OAuth registration, account consent, minimal operation scopes and credential refresh/revoke. This recipe adds no credential storage, OAuth flow or authentication fallback.
The retained source checkpoint and local protocol tests do not establish public package availability, live Google access, current account authorization or complete host adoption.
